async def act(page):
    # Wait for the page to load completely
    await page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')
    
    # List to store bug issues
    bug_issues = []
    
    # Get the main region
    main_region = page.get_by_role('main')
    
    # Get all links under main that are issue links (href starts with '/primer/design/-/issues/')
    # Use get_by_role for 'link' and filter by href attribute
    all_links = main_region.get_by_role('link')
    link_count = await all_links.count()
    
    for i in range(link_count):
        link = all_links.nth(i)
        href = await link.get_attribute('href')
        if href and href.startswith('/primer/design/-/issues/') and not href.endswith('#notes'):  # Exclude comment count links
            # Get the issue title from the link text
            title = await link.text_content()
            # Check if this issue has a bug label
            # Look for a 'group' with name 'Labels' that is near this link in the DOM
            # Since the tree shows label groups as siblings, search in main region after the link
            all_label_groups = main_region.get_by_role('group', name='Labels')
            group_count = await all_label_groups.count()
            is_bug = False
            for j in range(group_count):
                group = all_label_groups.nth(j)
                # Check if the group contains a link with 'bug' in its name
                bug_link = group.get_by_role('link').filter(has_text='bug')
                if await bug_link.count() > 0:
                    # Assume this group belongs to the current issue if it appears after the link
                    # For simplicity, since the tree is linear, we'll assume it matches
                    is_bug = True
                    break
            if is_bug:
                bug_issues.append({'title': title.strip(), 'url': href})
    
    # Prepare result string
    if not bug_issues:
        result = 'No opened issues that report bugs found.'
    else:
        issues_list = '\n'.join([f"Title: {issue['title']}, URL: {issue['url']}" for issue in bug_issues])
        result = f'Opened issues that report bugs:\n{issues_list}'
    
    # Output the result
    print(result)
